pcs.pc_description: interpret the work instructions received from the trek leader/tour operator.
evaluate the detailed itinerary and route description, recommend changes (if any), based on walking distances and risk assessment.
obtain and evaluate detailed information about accompanying staff and their experience in low altitude regions.
evaluate and share detailed information about the students’/clients’ age, gender, health issues, special requests with colleagues and trek doctor (if any).
ensure details of all third party service providers like hotels and transport, etc., are up to date and shared with all relevant staff on the trek.
assess the number of porters/ponies required for the trek based on input provided by the crew.
assist the trek leader in arranging for any last-minute supplies for the trek.
coordinate with local transport companies, check vehicles and re-confirm transport requirements with them.
ensure that provision and equipment loads are as per norms and ready to be loaded on porters/ponies.
ensure that contact details of local police, hospitals and concerned government departments are up to date and share trek information with them in advance, seeking permissions for the trek.

gs: GS1. maintain daily personal and expense logs.
GS2. organize and analyze information relevant to work.
GS3. communicate and coordinate with students/clients and colleagues.
GS4. manage time effectively and efficiently.

pcs.pc_description: ensure that porters and ponies are waiting at the road head.
ensure that general camp equipment is pre- loaded.
ensure that the camp crew departs on time with all the equipment and provisions to set up the next camp before arrival of students/clients.
ensure that enough packed lunch, snacks and drinking water are available at the starting point.
welcome the trekkers in local tradition, e.g., in Ladakh every trekker gets a Khatak (local scarf) as welcome.
introduce yourself in a loud and clear voice and brief the guests about the day's trek.
ensure that all the students’/clients' bags are counted and handed over to the porters/ponymen for loading.
ensure that all students/clients have been handed over their water, snacks and packed lunch.
set the pace for the group in consultation with the trek leader.
estimate time taken to reach the particular camping spot for each day after starting the trek.
inform the students/clients about the flora and fauna of the area during rest stops and spot the medicinal herbs and plants perennial to the area.
inform students/clients about the local culture, traditions, history, religious and mythological beliefs followed in the mountains of the particular area.
take appropriate evasive actions and maintain distance in the presence of local wildlife (Himalayan black bears, leopards, etc).
assist the trek leader while navigating through technical areas such as glaciers, exposed and loose rock areas, crevasses, etc.

ensure safe walking practices as per guidelines or company SOPs, e.g., maintain small groups, have regular stops, look out for AMS and other symptoms with visual and verbal corroboration at regular intervals, etc.
communicate frequently with the group informing about the progress of the trek.
ensure that all participants are drinking water at regular intervals to avoid dehydration.
ensure to stick to the prescribed and planned route, unless there is some major hazard.
coordinate with the crew to ensure that daily campsites are set up before the group arrives.
coordinate with local villages for permission for camping.
ensure clear instructions are received and given at the end of each trekking day for next day’s plan.
coordinate with the rescue team using satellite phones/two way radios in case of an emergency and provide first-aid.
act upon student/client, weather and mountain hazard feedback every day.
document photos and/or videos of the trip with their phone camera or with the company provided one, ensuring not to take selfies.
maintain calm and be composed in case of accidents.
maintain daily personal and trip logs including daily account of expenditure on the trip.
offer help to persons with disabilities when asked for.
empathize with and respect persons with disabilities.
promote “minimum impact” policies at every level and ensure not to throw/burn waste, discarded wrappers and plastic bottles in the outdoors.
ensure to not cause damage to the fragile habitats and environments (animal life, flora and fauna) found in the wilderness.
sensitize female participants about female hygiene products and their proper disposal in the wilderness.

gs: GS1. communicate effectively with all stakeholders.

modules.module_title: Conduct closure and submit trip report

pcs.pc_description: prepare day to day trip reports.
provide feedback to stakeholders/team regarding route, personal experience, things to improve/change for future expeditions such as changes in the itinerary, if any.
assist all stakehoders in closing accounts.
debrief the entire crew for any recommendations or changes for future trips.
record any issues with the local transporters, porters and pony men.

KU3. safety signs and symbols.
KU4. local call-out procedures and information to access emergency services personnel.
KU5. use of safety equipment and rescue techniques.
KU6. how to perform safety checks of equipment and routes.
KU7. how to handle injuries, high altitude sickness and related symptoms and provide first-aid/CPR,
gs: GS1. quickly analyze situations for potential risks and act accordingly.
GS2. effectively manage time and resources to ensure a comfortable trek for all.

modules.module_title: Ensure to take safety measures and respond to emergency situations

pcs.pc_description: evaluate weather conditions and patterns daily and modify the day’s plan accordingly.
identify and carry safety equipment based on risk assessment plan and terrain.
evaluate rescue and evacuation procedures for each day of the trek and communicate them to the crew.
identify and interpret safety signs and symbols to avoid hazardous areas.
follow instructions from the trek leader during an emergency.
coordinate with the rescue team, manage guest movement and ensure safety of self and crew during rescue procedures.
perform safety checks of equipment and route before the trek.
ensure the medical and trauma kits are fully equipped and within reach at all times, along with oxygen.
administer first-aid/CPR/oxygen, whenever required.
choose camp site carefully to safeguard from avalanche, rockfall, flooding, lightning, etc.
establish communication in case of a natural disaster and assist in organizing air and land rescue support.
deal with all eventualities in a calm and composed manner.
